intended_object: The induction functor Ind_G^H : Rep_k(G) ⥤ Rep_k(H) along a group homomorphism φ : G → H, sending A to k[H] ⊗_{k[G]} A with its H-action and acting on morphisms by id ⊗ f (from the docstring and the module documentation).
explanation: On objects the functor gives (k[H] ⊗_k A)_G, the coinvariants for the diagonal G-action, with g acting on k[H] by left multiplication by φ(g). These coinvariants are k[H] ⊗_{k[G]} A, and H acts by h·⟦h₁⊗a⟧ = ⟦h₁h⁻¹⊗a⟧. Up to h ↦ h⁻¹, this is the textbook induced representation, valid for any homomorphism φ. On morphisms it uses the map that id ⊗ f induces on coinvariants, which is well defined because f is G-equivariant. The same file proves the expected adjunction: induction is left adjoint to restriction. The setting (a commutative ring k, groups G and H, any homomorphism φ) is the natural one, and the construction needs inverses in H. Mathlib has no other, more general version.
